purpose: PBKDF2 Derive KAT (SP 800-132), tests PKCS#11 CKM_PKCS5_PBKD2 (C_DeriveKey).

_provenance.note: Replaces a file with zero _provenance ('Generated via Node.js crypto (OpenSSL backend), PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 and PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512' - self-generated, Tier 4, never admissible per this plan's ladder). NIST's PBKDF-1.0 algorithm is registered as PBKDF (SP 800-132), not 'KDF-Component' or a name under KDF-1.0 - confirmed against the ACVP-Server tree's real folder names at this pinned commit rather than guessed (gen-val/json-files/PBKDF-1.0/, sibling to KDF-1.0 and the separate kdf-components-* families, which cover TLS/SSH/IKEv2/etc. KDFs, not PBKDF2). This pinned commit's internalProjection.json has exactly ONE test group, hmacAlg=SHA2-224 (a real property of this specific commit's randomized generation, not a selection choice - there is no SHA2-256/384/512 group to pick from here). Engine constraints checked before selecting cases: C++ (SoftHSM_keygen.cpp:2883-2891) supports PRF HMAC-SHA1/224/256/384/512 and caps derived key length at 512 bytes (SoftHSM_keygen.cpp:2905, 'pbkdKeyLen > 512' rejected); Rust (ffi.rs:8686, 8699-8709) supports only HMAC-SHA256/384/512 (no SHA1, no SHA224) and additionally floors iterations at 1000 ('iterations < 1000' rejected). Net effect: this pinned commit's only real ACVP PBKDF2 evidence (SHA2-224) exercises the C++ engine only - Rust's PRF match arm (ffi.rs:8699-8709) has no SHA224 case at all (its constants.rs defines CKP_PBKDF2_HMAC_SHA256/384/512 only, no ...SHA224), so there is currently no real-ACVP-backed PBKDF2 coverage for the Rust engine in this repo; that is a genuine evidence gap to flag, not something this file can paper over by relabeling a SHA2-224 vector as SHA2-256. Three cases selected, all with iterationCount >= 1000 (keeping them clear of Rust's floor even though SHA224 itself isn't Rust-supported, in case that changes) and byte-aligned keyLen: tcId 37 (smallest derived key, 14 bytes, good for quick sanity reading), tcId 1 and tcId 7 (larger, more typical derived-key sizes). Independently re-verified all three against Python's hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac('sha224', password.encode('utf-8'), bytes.fromhex(salt), iterationCount, dklen=keyLen//8) immediately before writing this file - 3/3 byte-exact matches. Wired into the test harness: tests/helpers.mjs's pbkdf2() previously hardcoded PRF=CKP_PKCS5_PBKD2_HMAC_SHA512 (used only for a dk1==dk2 determinism self-check, acvp-wasm.mjs test #17 - never compared against a real expected value), so it now takes an explicit prf parameter (default unchanged, so test #17 is unaffected) and a new KAT block (#17.5) in acvp-wasm.mjs derives against tcId 1 here and compares to derivedKey.
